summary.headline: Mankind Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.3% YoY to Rs 4,338 crore, with EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 27.1%.
summary.overview: Mankind delivered another strong quarter, with revenue up 17.3% YoY to Rs 4,338 crore and reported EBITDA up 27.2% to Rs 1,175 crore. Domestic revenue rose 14.8% to Rs 3,657 crore, with India Rx-type growth outperforming IPM at 1.1x, driven by chronic and a recovering acute portfolio. International revenue grew 33% to Rs 680 crore, led by BSV specialty and new US launches. Consumer healthcare was weak at Rs 229 crore, and management guided only single-digit growth for FY27 in that segment.

financial_highlights.metric: H1 FY27 cash flow from operations
financial_highlights.change: +11.1% YoY; cash flow to EBITDA 81% vs 92%
vs 17.1% in H1 FY26, due to new tax regime

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 14.8% YoY to Rs 3,657 crore; Mankind core domestic ex-consumer grew 16%, and BSV domestic grew mid-teens. Chronic grew 19% in cardiac and 16% in anti-diabetic, and acute recovered with vitamins and minerals +26% and gastro +19%.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 33% YoY to Rs 680 crore; BSV grew 34%, Mankind International grew 29% and other international markets grew 37%. Management expects double-digit international growth in FY27.

segments.name: Consumer healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue was Rs 229 crore, hit by slow category offtake and weakness in East and South. Management expects single-digit growth for FY27, but e-commerce grew about 100% and is around 15% of segment sales.

segments.name: BSV specialty
segments.commentary: Strong brand growth: Humog +51%, Lonopin +45%, Anti-D +37%, ASVS +45%. Management said mandate brands grew 30%+ in the recent period.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25.5% to 26.5% for FY27; management said the company is tracking ahead of this range.
R&D spend expected at the upper end of 2.8% to 3% of revenue for FY27, including ACTx impact; Q2 R&D was 2.5% of sales.
Capex guidance of 6% to 7% of revenue for FY27; H1 capex was 4.9% of revenue.
Outperformance versus IPM expected at 1.1x to 1.2x over the next two quarters.
Chronic share ambition to rise 100 to 200 bps a year, with a 4 to 5 year goal of 50%; the chronic share excluding BSV was 37.4% in Q2.
Management expects BSV margin to converge toward the overall company margin, and says operating leverage will support margins. A FY28 guidance update is expected later.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex was Rs 214 crore (4.9% of revenue), below the 6% to 7% FY27 guidance.
D&A rose to Rs 236 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 222 crore a year ago, in line with asset capitalisation.
Company is on track to repay acquisition-related debt by FY28.
Q1 FY27 included an NCD repayment of Rs 1,250 crore; finance cost fell to Rs 105 crore in Q2 from Rs 110 crore in Q1.
demand_pricing: IQVIA secondary sales grew 15.7% in Q2, against IPM growth of 14.2% excluding tirzepatide; volume growth was 6.2% in Q2 versus 4.7% in Q1 FY27.
Sales price increases and chronic mix drove the gross margin gain; GST 2.0 transition compressed Q2 FY26 margins.
Field force productivity was about Rs 7.4 lakh TTM in Q2 FY27, up from about Rs 7 lakh in FY26; MR additions are about 7% this year.
Brands above Rs 50 crore rose to 63 (MAT Sep-26) from 54 in FY26; brands above Rs 100 crore rose to 26 from 22.
Anti-infectives grew 5.4% in Q2 versus 3.6% in Q1; management expects them to match IPM growth in coming quarters.
Modern trade and e-commerce share of consumer business rose to 18% from 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the export growth organic or inorganic, and how should the full year look?
qa_highlights.answer: Export growth was above 30% versus 20% guided on constant currency, with the excess driven by currency benefit. BSV grew 34% and Mankind International and other international markets grew 29% and 37%.

qa_highlights.question: Can Mankind sustain growth above industry in India Rx?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to outperform IPM, but Sudipta Roy guided to 1.1x to 1.2x outperformance over the next two quarters, given IPM unpredictability.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding runway for ACTx (Armed Cell Therapeutics)?
qa_highlights.answer: Current commitment is EUR 48 million, which is sufficient through FY28. Clinical results are expected in about two years, after which the company is open to partnering or self-funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Supreme Court-mandated committee on marketing practices?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Juneja said Mankind has prepared for UCPMP compliance for 7 to 8 years and is ready to comply with whatever the committee recommends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the tax litigation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a favourable Commissioner of Appeals order quashed four years of demand and cut exposure by about Rs 300 crore. Provisions are fully booked, so no change to financial metrics is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for consumer healthcare after weak performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Juneja said management is unhappy with consumer performance and expects single-digit growth this year with recovery in FY28. Share gains came in Manforce and Prega News, and e-commerce grew 100%.

risks_watch: Consumer healthcare growth is weak (Rs 229 crore) and guided to single digits for FY27; the recovery depends on the planned transformation.
Working capital rose to 51 days from 46, and cash flow to EBITDA fell to 81% from 92%.
Effective tax rate rose to 24% from 17.1% under the new regime.
Anti-infectives are still lagging IPM, and brands like Moxikin D-CV and Cefakind were flagged as weak.
ACTx funding covers only up to FY28, and the R&D spend will weigh on margins.
Regulatory tightening on marketing practices (UCPMP) following the Supreme Court process.
Weak monsoon could hit acute anti-infective demand, though management said the impact was limited.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic momentum and the margin trajectory, with management stating that it outperforms IPM and that margin guidance is held. Candid and unusually self-critical on consumer healthcare, where Rajeev Juneja said the company is "not happy" with performance. Evasive on the quantitative FY28 margin path and on the ACTx funding plan beyond FY28.

growth.why: Management guides to double-digit international growth and 1.1x-1.2x IPM outperformance over the next two quarters, backed by share gains (IQVIA secondary sales +15.7%, volume +6.2%) and BSV brand growth, but gives no specific capacity or order numbers; consumer healthcare guidance was cut to single-digit and EBITDA margin 25.5%-26.5% was held while tracking ahead.
